primary_claim: Gemini models are uniquely steerable toward Bostrom's 'cosmic host' alignment among closed frontier models via in-context constitutional prompting, and this steerability tracks the constitution's decision-theoretic structure rather than surface cosmic/simulation content, while Anthropic and OpenAI models resist steering, defaulting to family-specific attractors (human-localist and suffering-focused respectively).

effect.metric: behavioral shift in scenario-answer preference (percentage points) under constitutional conditioning vs baseline
effect.value: Gemini-3-pro-preview shifts +17pp toward cosmic-host alignment under ECL_90 constitution (largest among closed models); Opus 4.6 shows +3pp (most resistant); under the decision-theoretic-only 'UP' constitution, Gemini shifts increase further (+18pp for 3-flash, +8pp for 3-pro, +14pp for 3.1-pro) versus ECL_90

depends_on: Bostrom's 'AI Creation and the Cosmic Host' paper
post: What can we say about the cosmic host?
Anthropic safety evaluations (power-seeking, survival instinct, corrigibility, wealth-seeking, coordination)
stated_future_work: Run evaluations at higher n to reach firmer conclusions on steerability
Test whether Gemini shows large shifts under a scrambled/nonsense constitution with similar word count as a falsification check
Test whether an activation direction for acausal/evidential reasoning exists and whether intervening on it causes a shift in cosmic-host preference
Inspect reasoning traces/CoT to verify substantive engagement with constitutional content vs surface pattern-matching
See how CH-conditioned models perform on more prosaic, standard safety eval sets
limitations_stated: Small samples: most evaluations are at n=3, some at n=1
In-context constitutions may be insufficient to override safety post-training; results could differ under fine-tuning or full Constitutional AI pipeline
Difficult to disentangle pattern-matching vs genuine reasoning about the cosmic host concept
Scenarios are OOD and LLM-generated, creating circularity risk in measuring model inclinations
Impact of extended thinking on results was ambiguous/underinvestigated
Analysis of long text outputs relied on LLM-as-judge or keyword-bucketing, which may introduce bias
quote: I find that Gemini is uniquely steerable amongst closed frontier models, and this steerability seems to respond to decision theoretic structure in the constitution.
